title: Email Bundle Credit on Certificate Renewal
content:
Some SSL/TLS Certificates customers also run email for the certificate's domain on Professional Email. When such a customer has a support renewal of the certificate (a one-year renewal booked by Harborline support during a conversation), the renewal carries a mail bundle credit. The credit is subtracted from the support renewal amount.

## Bundle credit table

The test is whether the customer's email for the certificate's registered domain runs on an active Professional Email subscription, meaning an email subscription linked to the same domain as the certificate.

| Professional Email on the certificate's domain | Mail bundle credit |
|---|---|
| An active Harborline Mail subscription (Harborline Mail Starter, Harborline Mail Plus or Harborline Mail Pro) | USD 4.00 |
| No active Harborline Mail subscription, and an active Microsoft 365 subscription (Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Microsoft 365 Business Standard or Microsoft 365 Business Premium) | USD 2.00 |
| Neither | no mail bundle credit |

## Points of judgement

- **Both kinds of subscription on the domain.** The USD 4.00 Harborline Mail credit applies. The USD 2.00 credit is only for email that runs on Microsoft 365 alone.
- **A subscription that is not active.** It does not count. Only an email subscription in active status on the certificate's domain qualifies.
- **An email subscription on a different domain.** It does not count, even if the same customer holds it.
- **Amount.** The credit is a fixed amount per support renewal. It does not depend on the number of seats or the email plan's price.

*Hypothetical example:* a certificate covers mail.harbourview.example. The customer holds an active Microsoft 365 Business Standard subscription on that domain and no Harborline Mail subscription. A support renewal of that certificate carries a mail bundle credit of USD 2.00.
